analysis.evidence: Abram opens with בִּלְעָדַי, then uses רַק to allow for what the young men have eaten and for his companions’ share. הֵם יִקְחוּ חֶלְקָם (‘they shall take their share’) makes clear whose share he preserves.
analysis.morphology: The preposition takes a first-person common singular suffix referring to Abram.
analysis.sense: Abram excludes himself from receiving a share of the spoil.

analysis.evidence: After בִּלְעָדַי, Abram uses רַק to qualify his refusal. He makes an exception for what the young men ate and for the share due to the men who went with him.
analysis.morphology: Restrictive particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In רַק אֲשֶׁר אָכְלוּ הַנְּעָרִים, “only what the young men ate,” הַנְּעָרִים is the subject of אָכְלוּ. אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause with no expressed antecedent and identifies what they ate.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר אָכְלוּ הַנְּעָרִים means “what the young men ate.” Abram excepts what they have already consumed from the goods he declines to take.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural. The ending וּ agrees with the plural subject הַנְּעָרִים.

analysis.evidence: Abram sets aside what the young men ate during the expedition. He then claims a separate share for his named allies, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. The young men are Abram’s own fighting party.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine plural absolute noun. The dagesh in נ marks the doubling caused by the article.
analysis.sense: young men serving as fighting men
